results.why: Deck B is the tighter control shell: four Lightning Helix, three Get Lost, two Day of Judgment and four No More Lies give it plenty of cheap interaction to survive until Lute turns on Jeskai Revelation and Inevitable Defeat. Its mana has real dual and Verge support for all four colors. Deck A plays one-ofs like Flashback, Erode and Mystical Teachings plus clunky 7-drop Capstones, and has less early interaction, so it is clearly the less consistent build.

Deck A is a cleaner Jeskai-plus-black control shell, with full playsets of the premium interaction (Lightning Helix, No More Lies, Inevitable Defeat) plus Get Lost, Three Steps Ahead and two sweepers. Its black splash leans on shocks, Gloomlake Verge and Great Hall, which is adequate. Deck B spreads itself across cute singletons (Flashback, Erode, Mystical Teachings) and clunky 7-drop Improvisation Capstones while cutting core removal and counters to 1–2 copies, making it less consistent despite a fourth Lute.

Deck B actually builds around all three requested cards. It runs four Jolly Balloon Man with real red sources (Stomping Ground, Sacred Foundry, Multiversal Passage, Spider Manifestation, Pollinator). Its mana-creature shell powers into Ouroboroid, Craterhoof and Gearhulk, and Balloon Man can copy any of them. Deck A plays a single Balloon Man with almost no red mana beyond Starting Town, and its Stormchaser's Talent/Boomerang pieces are a muddled plan around the request.

Deck A actually builds around all three requested cards: it runs 4 Jolly Balloon Man with real red sources, and Bloom Tender, mana dorks and Nature's Rhythm ramp into Gearhulk, Speaker and Craterhoof, all of which Balloon copies well. Deck B plays a single Jolly Balloon Man whose only red source is Starting Town. Its blue bounce/Otter shell drifts away from the request, and its mana is stretched across three colors.

Deck B is a tighter Dwarf-equipment shell. Cheap equipment like Hard-Won Jitte and Spider-Suit is cheap to cast and becomes nearly free to move with Mauler and Kíli, and Giott adds another double-striking Dwarf that loots off every Dwarf or Equipment entering. Deck A dilutes the plan with non-Dwarves like Mabel and Zack Fair, a heavier top end (Thorin, Mountain-king, Katana), and colour-restricted Cavern of Souls in a deck that wants to cast plenty of noncreature spells.

Deck A is a tight, all-Dwarf shell of 20 creatures. Cheap equipment like Hard-Won Jitte and Spider-Suit becomes nearly free with Mauler and Kíli, Giott adds card filtering on every Dwarf or Equipment entering, and 7 burn spells give real interaction. Deck B is solid but dilutes the plan with off-theme singletons (Mabel, Zack, Bofur), runs only 4 removal spells, and its 4 Cavern of Souls produce only colorless mana for its burn and Katana.

Deck B is a tight mono-black aristocrats shell. Recursive fodder (Bloodghast, Forsaken Miner, Nine-Lives Familiar, Infestation Sage) feeds Zealot and Sackville, and Popular Egotist gives a real drain payoff. Its many crime enablers (Sackville and Egotist triggers, Hex, Sheriff, Talent) keep Miner looping, all on perfect mono-color mana. Deck A's sac fodder is mostly one-shot, it leans on a clunky 4-mana Raise the Past, and it dilutes the plan with Amalia lifegain and Queen of Dale, so it lacks a strong sacrifice payoff.

Deck A builds a real aristocrats engine around the three requested cards. Umbral Collar Zealot is a free sac outlet. Bloodghast, Forsaken Miner and Nine-Lives Familiar give recursive fodder. Popular Egotist and The Sackville-Bagginses target opponents, which counts as committing crimes, so Miner keeps coming back as a repeatable drain loop, with clean mono-black mana. Deck B is a lifegain/Amalia/Raise the Past deck that only loosely uses the sacrifice package, so its pieces pull in different directions.

Deck B runs full playsets of Gideon's Memorial and Solitary Cell alongside Ajani Unrelenting. Its 24-land R/W manabase is clean, and its cheap interaction (Burst Lightning, Sear, Get Lost) plus Voice of Victory protects its planeswalkers coherently. Deck A runs only 2 Solitary Cell and a clunky 25-land manabase full of tapped and colorless utility lands (Sunken Citadel, Fountainport, Demolition Field). Its Day of Judgment also cuts against the token synergies the Memorial wants.

Deck A has a cleaner two-color mana base: 24 lands, all producing R or W, plus basics that enable Sunbillow Verge. It also adds Voice of Victory as a cheap token producer that synergizes with Gideon's Memorial alongside efficient removal. Deck B runs too many colorless or tapped utility lands (Demolition Field, Fountainport, Sunken Citadel) for a deck needing RR and WW, and its Day of Judgment works against its own token plan.

Deck B packs real synergy around Trudge. Kiora's untap strips stun counters, and Ouroboroid pumps a big Trudge or Henge-boosted board every combat. Kiora and Outcaster Trailblazer turn every 4+ power creature into card draw, so it refuels while ramping toward Fight Rigging's 7-power threshold. Deck A leans on Hammerskull and three clunky hard-cast Ulamogs, a less focused ramp pile with weaker payoffs for the requested cards.

Deck A runs a coherent Trudge/Henge ramp shell. Ouroboroid and Fight Rigging push creatures to 7+ power easily, and Outcaster Trailblazer plus Kiora turn every big creature into a card. Kiora's untap also strips stun counters off Trudge or untaps Nykthos. Deck B leans on clunky 3x Ulamog and 4 colorless Nykthos with Hammerskull as filler, so it has less card flow and a more top-heavy curve that loses to disruption.

Deck B is a coherent mono-white heroic shell. Phalanx Leader, Illuminator Virtuoso and Hero of Iroas all reward the cheap targeting spells, and Gods Willing, Feat of Resistance and Sejiri Shelter protect the threats. Its mana is clean, with only minor Mutavault tension against WW costs. Deck A splashes red for Academic Dispute and Reckless Rage, which don't fit a heroic plan, and it has only Hoplite as a real payoff for Guiding Voice and Practiced Offense.

Deck A is a focused mono-white heroic shell: Phalanx Leader, Illuminator Virtuoso and Hero of Iroas all reward the cheap targeting spells, and it has protection spells to keep threats alive. Its mono-W mana is clean apart from a small Mutavault/WW tension. Deck B has few heroic payoffs beyond Hoplite, plays filler like Academic Dispute, and spreads into two colors for little synergy gain.

Deck B is a coherent Jeskai control shell with counters, cheap removal, sweepers and Stock Up. Its black splash for Inevitable Defeat has about nine sources, and its manabase supports all three of Jeskai Revelation's colors well. Deck A stretches into four colors with Languish, Thoughtseize and Shoot the Sheriff while leaning on few real blue sources for Stock Up, Consult the Star Charts and Revelation, so its mana is far shakier.

Deck A is a coherent Jeskai control shell with a light black splash. Jeskai Revelation, Stock Up, Consult and No More Lies all get reliable blue from shocks, Verges and Triomes, while about nine black sources are enough for Inevitable Defeat. Deck B is a Mardu base that thinly splashes blue for its two key blue cards (Revelation and Stock Up), leaning on Great Hall, Starting Town and conditional Riverpyre Verges. That makes its marquee 7-drop and card draw shakier, and it lacks the counters and sweepers that make A's long-game plan hang together.

Deck A is a coherent Simic shell where Bushwhack fits naturally. It has ample green sources and basics to fetch, and Up the Beanstalk turns every discounted Terror, Crab and This Town into card draw. Deck B is essentially Izzet Terror with a strained green splash: about eight green sources, several of them tapped or conditional, for four one-mana sorceries that its burn-heavy plan barely needs.

Deck A is a coherent Izzet-Terror shell splashing green for Bushwhack. It has 37 cheap instants and sorceries to power out Terror and Crab and real interaction in Fiery Impulse, Burst Lightning, Axe and Critique, while the 19-land mana base gives enough red and green sources. Deck B's Beanstalk and Town synergies are cute, but it plays 8 non-spell enchantments that slow its cost reduction and relies almost entirely on Bushwhack fights and bounce for interaction, which is too thin for Pioneer.

Deck B treats Lorehold as a real build-around, running three copies alongside a burn suite (Burst Lightning, Lightning Helix, Charring Bite) that benefits from its miracle and looting. Nova Hellkite's warp feeds repeated Dragon-enter triggers for Sarkhan and Momo, and the manabase (Pathways, Sundown Pass) is smoother than Deck A's six Mountains. Deck A has strong individual cards like Draconic Roar, but its single Lorehold barely meets the request, and filler like Monstrous Rage and Dragon Engine weakens the plan.

Deck A actually builds around all three requested cards, running 3 Lorehold alongside 9 instants and Charring Bite so the miracle and looting text matters. Nova Hellkite's warp pairs well with Momo and Sarkhan, and the 24-land Boros manabase is clean. Deck B is a solid dragon-aggro shell with Draconic Roar, but it relegates Lorehold to a one-of and adds Smaug treasures that fight its own 4 Clarion Conqueror.

Deck B is a coherent Rakdos Persist/Archon shell. Faithless Looting and the free sac outlets bin Archon and get it back, and Eyetwitch, Supplier and Bloodghast double as free Flare of Malice fodder. That makes all four Flares strong, and the mana is clean. Deck A plays only one Flare despite the request and spreads itself across Emperor, Dissident, Hexmage tricks and Street Wraith hardcasting, so it is less focused.

Deck A plays four Flare of Malice alongside Eyetwitch, Stitcher's Supplier and Bloodghast as free sacrifice fodder. Looting and Persist reanimate Archon, so the plan is focused and has a functional Rakdos manabase. Deck B runs only one Flare of Malice despite the request, and it spreads itself across Emperor of Bones, Trawler, Dissident and Hexmage, so its graveyard plan is diluted and less coherent.

Deck A follows the proven Eldrazi Ramp shell. Fanatic of Rhonas, Green Sun's Zenith (with Dryad Arbor) and Disciple/Garden give it fast, redundant green ramp, and Fanatic's ferocious mode pairs naturally with a big Slumbering Trudge or Fight Rigging target. Deck B leans on clunkier ramp like Talisman of Impulse and Utopia Sprawl with only nine Forests, and its Sire/Cavern/Shifting Woodland package is weaker than A's tighter payoff suite of Emrakul and Devourer.

Deck B's ramp plan hangs together better: Fanatic of Rhonas turns on its ferocious ability off a Slumbering Trudge or a Fight Rigging-boosted creature. Green Sun's Zenith gives extra copies of Trudge, Fanatic and Dryad Arbor, and the Turntimber and Disciple double-faced cards keep the land count high without flooding. Deck A splits its mana between Utopia Sprawl (only 9 Forests to enchant), Halfling and Talisman, and runs a thinner top end of a lone Devourer and 2 Sire, so its payoffs feel less focused.

Deck A is built around the engine itself: Gamble, LED, Does Machines and Riddlesmith loots all bin Echo of Eons for cheap flashback. Baubles, Moxen and Petals feed Riddlesmith and recur Daredevil, with Urza's Saga, Defense Grid and Grapeshot/Ominous Harvest rounding out a coherent artifact-storm shell. Deck B is mostly a TES list with the requested cards stapled on and few ways to discard Echo besides LED, so its Echo plan often means hard-casting a six-drop.

Deck A has a sound storm skeleton: Dark Ritual, Infernal Tutor, Tendrils, LED and Paradoxical Outcome all work with Riddlesmith looting and Echo flashback. Its 13-land UB mana base reliably casts its spells, and it gives Daredevil a real presence. Deck B's mana is thin and awkward: Ancient Tomb is colorless, red comes only from 2 Volcanic Islands plus fast mana for 4 Gamble, and blue sources are few. Its kill (one Grapeshot or Ominous Harvest) is shakier, and it includes Daredevil only as a token single copy.

Deck B builds a real Arclight Phoenix engine. It runs four Phoenixes, Buried Alive to bin them, and free or cheap instants (Mutagenic Growth, Gut Shot, Lava Dart with flashback, Looting) to hit three spells in a turn. Its mana supports all three colors through Mire, Delta and three dual types. Deck A dilutes the plan with only three Phoenixes, The One Ring, Wasteland and Thoughtseize, and gives Bolt and Looting only two red sources.

Deck A is a focused Phoenix combo shell. Buried Alive dumps up to three Phoenixes, and free or cheap spells (Mutagenic Growth, Gut Shot, Lava Dart, Dark Ritual, Lotus Petal) reliably reach three instants and sorceries for a hasty, flying return, while Faithless Looting and Flow State dig toward the pieces. Deck B dilutes the plan with The One Ring, Wasteland and a Daze/Thoughtseize tempo shell, has fewer cheap spells to trigger Phoenix, and supports four Lightning Bolt and Looting with only two Volcanic Islands as red sources.

Deck B is a coherent Boros artifact-aggro shell. Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher combo with Springleaf Drum and the artifact lands, metalcraft powers both Ardent Recruit and Galvanic Blast, and Bolt plus Journey give it real interaction. Deck A goes wide cohesively but has zero removal, and it plays filler like Phyrexian Walker, which makes it far worse against the field.

Deck B is a tight mono-white go-wide build. Free bodies like Ornithopter and Phyrexian Walker turn on Springleaf Drum, Search Party Captain and Salt Road Packbeast refill the hand, and Spider-Man, Leonardo, Martyr's Soul and Ramosian Rally all reward a wide board. Deck A has nice removal, but its 18 lands plus Drum are too much mana for a curve that tops out at Captain, and it has fewer creatures to fuel Drum and Captain.

Deck A has a real engine. Looting, Pursue the Past and Thrilling Discovery fuel graveyard recursion: Sneaky Snacker returns when you draw a third card, every multicolored sorcery brings the Eidolons back, and each card leaving the graveyard grows Spirit Mascot. Tireless Tribe plus Inside Out adds a combo kill. Deck B is a generic Boros aggro list where the 4-mana Eidolons are clunky filler with few multicolored triggers to recur them, so it doesn't build around the requested cards nearly as well.

Deck B builds a real graveyard engine around the requested cards. Looting, Thrilling Discovery and Pursue the Past discard Eidolons and Sneaky Snackers, which come back via multicolored spells and third-card draws, so Spirit Mascot keeps growing. Tireless Tribe plus Inside Out adds a cheap, hybrid-castable finisher. Deck A is a generic Boros aggro pile where the Eidolons are clunky four-drops with little discard to fuel their recursion.

Deck A is a coherent Explorer/Rector control shell. Therapy, Innocent Blood and Phyrexian Tower trigger Explorer and Rector. The Explorer ramp powers out Decree of Silence and Future Sight, and Rector finds Decree, Future Sight or Deed, all backed by Fact or Fiction, Impulse and Swords on a sensible four-color manabase. Deck B is a stretched five-color Survival toolbox where Future Sight is incidental, the red and black splashes are thin, and many one-of creatures dilute the requested plan.

Deck B is the real Rector-Explorer control shell. Explorer ramps into Future Sight and Decree of Silence, which Rector can also tutor. Therapy, Innocent Blood and Phyrexian Tower trigger the death effects, while Deed, Swords, FoF and Gaea's Blessing make a coherent four-color control plan on solid mana. Deck A is a stretched five-color Survival toolbox where Future Sight is an awkward UUU add-on, and Explorer just ramps the opponent with no real payoff to punish it.

Deck A is a coherent Survival/Sneak Attack shell: Survival finds Dragon Tyrant, Colossus or Bolas, and Sneak Attack ignores their colored costs, giving it a real one-turn kill backed by Fling, Genesis and the Squee/Therapy engine. Deck B plays the requested cards as four-ofs, but its main reanimation target is a 6/6 for 8 life whose sacrifice ability also hits its own pilot. With only a single Symbiotic Wurm as backup, it lacks a convincing finisher.

Deck A builds a real Premodern reanimator shell around the requested cards. It runs full playsets of Utopia Tree, Rhystic Tutor and Bloodfire Colossus, with Buried Alive, Survival, Putrid Imp and Exhume/Reanimate/Animate Dead plus Dark Ritual and Lotus Petal for fast, focused starts. Deck B treats Colossus and Rhystic Tutor as afterthoughts (1 and 2 copies) and stretches its mana for Nicol Bolas (UU) and Phantom Nishoba (W) with few sources, making a clunkier, less coherent pile.
